explanation: Invert both subtrees recursively and exchange the two child links at each original node. Values and node identities stay unchanged.
timeComplexity: O(n) time for n nodes. Every node is visited once and exchanges two child references.
spaceComplexity: O(h) recursion space for tree height h. Only the active root-to-node recursion chain of height h is retained.
attribution: Original EPI Practice C# implementation, reusing and refining the repository-authored Blind75 algorithm fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: A null subtree is already inverted. Assuming both child subtrees are recursively inverted, exchanging their links places every original left-descendant path at its mirrored right-descendant path and vice versa. Induction proves the whole tree is mirrored while node identities and values stay unchanged.
walkthrough: For [4,2,8,1,3,6,9], swap root children 2 and 8. Recursively swap 1 with 3 under node 2 and 6 with 9 under node 8. The resulting level-order tree is [4,8,2,9,6,3,1]. Expected is the mutated original tree in level order; the returned root and every node must retain original identity.
edgeCases: Newly allocated replacement nodes violate the identity contract.
